claims.summary: Portuguese Brazilian uses 'ele/ela' as direct object, while standard Spanish expects an unstressed pronoun like 'lo/la'.
Common constructions in Brazilian Portuguese include 'vi ele', 'conheço ela', and 'encontrei eles'. Formal written Portuguese may prefer 'o/a/os/as'.
Portuguese spoken: 'Eu vi ele.'; Portuguese formal: 'Eu o vi.'; Spanish: 'Lo vi.'; Portuguese: 'Conheço ela há anos.'
Direct object forms in Portuguese should not be translated word-for-word as Spanish direct objects, as the syntactic function differs.
